text:
Elena Park: tossing two small entry patterns for first-run that try not to scream at users: (A) a muted prompt strip pinned to the top (thin, single-line CTA) and (B) an expandable sample card inline next to the projects list (card expands to show 3 starter samples). Figma: https://fig.redwood/f/onboard/prompt_strip and https://fig.redwood/f/onboard/expand_card. which do we prototype?
Ravi (Design): i like the expandable card for discoverability 1 it's more visual. strip is much friendlier for power users who want less interruption.
Sam (Eng): strip is trivial (one banner, single CTA). expandable card needs JS for expand/collapse, image lazy-loading, and careful animation to avoid layout shift. also card needs an accessible collapse state.
Kaya (Growth): per prior tests, thin persistent prompts get more eyeballs but lower downstream action; richer visual components lift exploration metrics. recommendation: experiment both with conversion funnel: impression -> open sample -> project created.
Mei (a11y): accessibility notes up front:
- strip: must be reachable by keyboard, announce via aria-live when it appears, include clear dismiss ("hide for now") with aria-label.
- card: use button with aria-expanded and aria-controls for the expanded region; expanded content should be placed inline (not via portal) so screen readers follow flow; images need meaningful alt text.
Ravi (Design): copy options (fresh wording):
```
Variant X headline: "Spin up a demo in 30 seconds"
CTA X: "Try demo"

Variant Y headline: "Browse starter apps and templates"
CTA Y: "See samples"

Variant Z headline: "Quickstart with an example project"
CTA Z: "Quickstart"
```
Sam (Eng): my vote: strip -> "Try demo" (short), card -> "See samples" (discovery). keep Z as fallback.
Kaya (Growth): prefer Variant X for the strip (time promise helps), Variant Y for the card. recommend A/B X vs Z on strip if we want to squeeze more lift.
Mei (a11y): contrast nit: current strip CTA color in comp only meets 3.3:1. needs at least 4.5:1 for small text. card thumbnails also need 1:1 alt fallback. i'll add explicit a11y acceptance criteria.
Elena Park: agreed. action plan: 1) Ravi update comps with elevated contrast + aria notes 2) Sam stub feature flag and implement strip + card behind flag (45% strip / 45% card / 10% control) 3) Mei run quick a11y smoke on staging 4) Kaya wire metrics + dashboards (onboard.impression, onboard.open, onboard.sample_start, project.create).
Sam (Eng): will implement expand/collapse with reduced-motion support and aria-expanded. will persist "don't show again" per-user. creating ticket: ONB-721.
ExperimentBot: Created experiment exp.onboard.prompt_card_vs_strip.v1 with rollout 45% strip / 45% card / 10% control.
Kaya (Growth): power calc: ~2k new orgs per arm for 3pp detection on create rate. i'll post expected ETA once cohort size available.
Mei (a11y): checklist i'll run after Ravi uploads updated frames: keyboard nav, screen reader announce for appear/expand/collapse, focus order, dismiss semantics, contrast. posting results here.
Ravi (Design): uploading revised frames to Figma and adding a11y annotations by EOD. tagging @eng-squad for implementation details.
Elena Park: thanks everyone 1 let's review after 7 days of running the experiment. will follow up with a short notes doc and next steps.
Sam (Eng): FYI i added a small analytics debounce to prevent double impressions when user navigates quickly.
Kaya (Growth): tagging @support to monitor any spike in onboarding questions during rollout.
Elena Park: closing loop for now. :party:
